Small-town America is struggling in comparison to urban areas, but we would still be in a dire situation without the agriculture (and trucking, oh the trucking) that we rely on from rural communities.

The rural southern areas often emphasize self-sufficiency—creating your own solutions and taking care of oneself. This mindset contrasts sharply with urban life. One thing I wish was still prevalent is a strong local business culture—despite the anti-urban sentiment, people still seem to have a fondness for their large retail chains.

I don't know. The southern region presents an intriguing paradox.
